style.summary:
style of A: Curious and questioning, with short, direct questions.
style of B: Expert and explanatory, using Well and So to organize a measured answer.

A: A's question-asking tone lets A set what B has to explain.
A's short, direct question forces B to answer in full.
A's opening remark that it is just easier to do sets a framing B has to qualify.
B: B's expert tone with Well and So presents B as the authority on the procedure.
B's assurance that the test is completely fair sets the terms for the evaluation.
B's detailed answer carries the technical weight of the exchange.

A: A's question is brief, and B's expansive answer decides what the group learns about the procedure.
A's forcing of a full answer depends on B choosing to give one, so B controls the depth.
A's framing that it is easier is immediately qualified by B, so B sets the terms.
B: B's expertise only matters if A accepts the procedure, and A's question shows A is testing it.
B's assurance of fairness is conditional on the new segmentations working, so A's test decides.
B's answer is detailed but responds to A's question, so A decides which details matter.

content.summary:
content of A: Asks how the data are grouped together.
content of B: Explains grouping by channel and Thilo's speech detector, and how cross-talk is handled.

A: A's question about grouping determines the topic B addresses.
A's focus on how grouping is determined drives the exchange onto procedure.
A's opening point frames the choice of method as easier.
B: B's explanation of grouping by channel and speech detector is the substantive content.
B's statement that cross-talk is processed as the speaker's data adds technical detail.
B's point about the new test being fair concerns the central validity question.

A: A raises the topic, but B's explanation supplies everything the group actually learns.
A's focus on procedure is only a question, while B determines the method used.
A's ease claim is undercut by B's new test, so B decides which method stands.
B: B's grouping rule is the procedure A asked about, so it is only what A's question requested.
Cross-talk handling depends on the speaker assumption A is questioning, so A holds the critical point.
The fairness claim depends on segmentations A has yet to see working, so A decides.

coordination.summary:
coordination of A: Uses short turns and asks a question to hand the floor to B.
coordination of B: Holds the longer turn and answers fully, organizing it with Well and So.

A: A chooses the moment to ask the question, which hands B the next turn.
A's short turns keep the exchange focused on A's question.
A's interjection It's just easier to do opened the topic.
B: B holds the longer turn and controls the answer's length.
B's Well and So signal that B is organizing the turn.
B holds the explanation until the end.

A: A's question hands the turn over, but B decides how long the answer runs.
A's short turns only work because B gives space for them, so B controls the pacing.
A's opening was a comment that B picked up and reframed, so B set the topic.
B: B's long answer responds to A's question, so A determines when it starts and what it covers.
B's signposts respond to A's question, so A is effectively directing the turn.
B's explanation is held until A's question prompts it, so A controls when it is delivered.

engagement.summary:
engagement of A: Asks a follow-up question, showing curiosity about the method.
engagement of B: Offers detail and reassurance about the test, showing investment in its validity.

A: A asks a follow-up question, showing active curiosity.
A's focus on how grouping is determined shows genuine interest.
A's opening comment shows investment in the choice of method.
B: B offers detail and reassurance, showing investment in the test.
B's answer covers cross-talk, a sign of attention to edge cases.
B's statements that the test is fair show B cares about its validity.

A: A's question is a single prompt, while B's detail shows sustained engagement.
A's curiosity is real but narrow, while B's answer shows engagement with the whole procedure.
A's opening comment dismisses the choice, so A's investment is weaker than B's.
B: B's detail responds to A's question, so A's curiosity drives the depth of B's engagement.
B's care about fairness is conditional on the new segmentations, which A is still assessing.
B's edge-case attention is a reply to A's question, so A shapes where the engagement goes.
